evidence.quoted_text:
"manager_restarted": (
            (((manager.get("before") or {}).get("manager") or {})
             .get("pid") or 0) > 0
            and (((manager.get("after") or {}).get("manager") or {})
                 .get("pid") or 0) > 0
            and (manager.get("before") or {}).get("manager", {}).get("pid")
            != (manager.get("after") or {}).get("manager", {}).get("pid")
            and bool(((manager.get("before") or {}).get("manager") or {})
                     .get("invocation_id"))
            and bool(((manager.get("after") or {}).get("manager") or {})
                     .get("invocation_id"))
            and (manager.get("before") or {}).get("manager", {}).get("invocation_id")
            != (manager.get("after") or {}).get("manager", {}).get("invocation_id")),
evidence.reason: The manager_restarted check only requires positive and differing manager PIDs plus nonempty differing invocation IDs. It never compares boot IDs between the two manager snapshots. A guest reboot between those snapshots supplies a new boot with different PID and invocation IDs, so the check can falsely accept an isolated manager restart even though the observations span a reboot. Requiring nonempty equal boot IDs is a routine correctness repair, not a new contract requirement or owner decision.
